findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The top of the inside of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on the sides. CORRECTED- One of the PICs cleaned this during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned regularly and maintained clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to fill a container in the handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated and aware that handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a container of raw salmon above a container of cooked beef in the bottom of a preparation cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the PIC corrected the storage order (the salmon was moved below the beef in the cooler). Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The walk-in cooler fan has a leak coming from it that the PIC stated had just started today. The PIC discarded food items that were under it and moved others to protect them from contamination. Bins were placed under the leak until it can be repaired. The PIC stated that the walk-in cooler might be in defrost mode. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Inspector observed a staff member shutting off the sink without using a barrier after handwashing. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff members remember to use a barrier after to shut off the faucet in order to avoid recontaminating their hands. 


Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: THIS IS A THRICE REPEAT VIOLATION. There was no sanitizer bucket (s) available on the cook line at the beginning of today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. The sani bucket was made immediately. The final measured of the sanitizer concentration was 200 ppm. Ensure that sani buckets are made at the appropriate temperature at all times during food prep.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Inspector observed several food items in the walk-in cooler not properly date marked. Some of the items are but not limited to an opened jug of milk, sauces, dumplings fillings, cooked meat, and etc. PIC was made aware and education was carried out. Ensure that all food items are properly dated when they are being stored for future use. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.comment: Inspector observed staff donning gloves without washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to wash their hands in between tasks before donning gloves for food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

Observed several personal phones to be sitting on surfaces throughout the facility.(at least 3) Take care to store phones away from food and areas that are to remain clean for food preparation, food storage, or clean item storage.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Lights directly above butcher block in center of the kitchen have dust on top of them. Clean as needed to prevent dust build-up above a food prep area.
2. Both spray nozzles of the 3 compartment sink and dish machine areas have food build-up/moldy debris on the squeezer of the handle. Routinely clean the nozzles - wash, rinse, sanitize.

Discussed with PIC. Ensure routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces to prevent soil build-up. Clean by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed in-use rags being utilized with spray bottle of bleach. Rag cannot be stored in sanitizing solution. Cease practice. Utilize paper towels with the spray bottle of sanitizer and/or a sanitization bucket where the in-use rag is placed in an appropriate level of sanitizer solution when not used. Bleach: 50-200 ppm or Quat: 200-400 ppm. Discussed with employee and PIC. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

(REPEAT) Observed several areas of the facility where to-go containers were not protected against cross contamination (specifically salad prep table). Large pots in the back near the reach-in freezer should be inverted on the top shelf (flip over). Discussed with PIC. Food contact surfaces should be protected from cross contamination by inverting. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/4/21.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed lack of date marking on several food items throughout facility. Prep cooler on right wall near three compartment sink: chicken salad, blood mary mix, chicken liver mousse. All items lacked appropriate date marking; however, staff stated the items were made Monday, 3/1/21. Date marking was applied. A system was discussed regarding how to date mark to-go containers of said items. Ideas suggested were a date marking dry erase board on the outside of the prep cooler, date marking the display container of the food to indicate that particular food item row was prepped on said date. Facility will produce a satisfactory system for date marking to-go containers of RTE/TCS foods. Walk-in cooler: homemade pickles, cooled sweet potatoes and potatoes. Dates were added to all food items during inspection. COS.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned

Observed cups being utilized as scoops in the large dry storage containers (flours). Discussed ceasing practices with PIC. Scoops should have handles that are upright and not within food item. Observed multiple spoons immersed in room temperature water at the prep line. Spoons should be in a container of water that allows sufficient flow to move food debris and washed, rinsed, and sanitized frequently. Spoons were removed from immersed water during inspection. Inspector will create a Time as Public Health Control Policy to allow for spoons immersed in water at prep line. Spoons and container the spoons are held within will be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Observed to-go containers (top prep cooler near three compartment sink) and clean equipment on top of drying shelf (near left side of kitchen by hand sink) to not be covered or inverted in order to protect against cross-contamination of a food-contact surface. Discussed ceasing practice with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. 

Observed no thermometer in bottom prep cooler #1 near front house. PIC purchased thermometer during spot check. COS.
